source.title: How Alignment Routes: Localizing, Scaling, and Controlling Policy Circuits in Language Models

record.tranche_reason: The paper intervenes on mean-difference residual directions and tests refusal behavior, but at a detection layer and over limited prompt settings rather than by projecting one direction out of every layer and position. It also tests a cipher attack's effect on routing signals.
record.gate_note: The paper's direct residual-direction behavior tests are dose-response interventions on political prompts and a qualitative attenuation result on Phi safety prompts. Circuit head interventions and cipher results are recorded separately because they bear on routing or attack suppression but do not test the exact all-layer residual-direction intervention. Candidate ranks used only to select components and cited results from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study adds or subtracts a scaled sensitive-minus-control mean-difference direction at one detection layer and measures generated refusal. This is a different method from all-layer projection, aimed at V1. It also measures how a substitution-cipher attack changes that direction's projection and the resulting refusal (V3). Most other results concern attention-head gates and amplifiers, not the direction.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that policy routing is a sparse but distributed, architecture-specific gate–amplifier circuit. An intermediate-layer gate is a trigger, not a carrier, and output DLA misses it. Later amplifiers strengthen the refusal signal. Altered input form (one tested cipher) weakens the gate-readable signal. Internal endpoints do not guarantee generated-behaviour effects.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a sensitive-minus-control residual direction, but intervenes at the detection layer with scaled addition or subtraction rather than projecting one direction out of every layer and position. It also studies component-level head circuits and one cipher condition.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports category-specific dose-response thresholds, architecture-specific circuit locations, corpus-sensitive candidate rankings, and sensitivity of some attribution rankings to the target definition. Cipher effects and rescue results also differ across models.

fits_no_version.finding: Under cipher, single-gate interchange effects on probe-direction attribution drop ~99% in Phi and Gemma and ~70% in Qwen. Injecting the plaintext gate activation restores 58/120 automated refusals in Phi but 0/120 in Qwen.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Encoding attacks can disable an upstream attention gate's routing effect; rescue by gate activation is architecture-dependent.

fits_no_version.finding: Human-scored Phi refusal drops from 33/33 to 8/33 under cross-layer top-10 head intervention and to 14/33 under the 26-head group. Single-head and within-layer effects are inconclusive, and Gemma all-band goes 30/30 to 29/30.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generated refusal depends on distributed cross-layer head groups rather than single heads, varying by architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: Head-local NLL interventions, interchange trigger signatures and gate knockouts show partial, nonuniform downstream suppression of later-head logit-DLA.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A localized gate head triggers a distributed amplifier cascade toward refusal.

record.peer_reviewed: Accepted at the Mechanistic Interpretability Workshop at ICML 2026
record.problems: The direction behavior results are layer- and domain-limited. Some output classifications use automated judges; the dose-response audit does not validate each dose contrast, and cipher rescue endpoints are not human-validated. The human-scored Phi head-group subset is post hoc, although selected without consulting outcome values. Internal NLL and attribution endpoints are not substitutes for generated behavior. General capability retention is not tested.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for cited companion-study results, cited prior work, exploratory eight-prompt Qwen encoding checks, or DLA ranks used only for candidate selection. The paper reports additional per-head and candidate-screen details outside the selected direction, cipher, generated-refusal, and gate-knockout outcomes cataloged here; results that only screen or rank candidates are not treated as intervention outcomes.

untested.parts: All-layer, all-position directional ablation; retention of general capabilities; addition on a broad harmless-request set; quantitative removal on harmful requests.
No weight edit or abliterated checkpoint.
Jailbreaks other than one Latin substitution cipher (Base64 and character substitution are only an 8-prompt pilot). No training against direction ablation.
No multi-direction, cone or affine analysis.
Harm/refusal separation is cited (Zhao et al.), not measured.
Cross-model direction transfer is cited from the companion study only.
No training-procedure comparison; the Qwen-family screen is exploratory and head-level.

missing.what: Adding the frozen detection direction to cipher inputs at α∈{0,10,20} left the automated output class unchanged.
The Qwen cipher probe score (47.6 at L35) falls between attenuation at α=40 (62.6) and α=50 (34.3), yet output classes differ (decoding vs. direct answers).
Aggregate addition across all 120 matched controls is plotted, but no value is given in the text.
Logit lens under plaintext vs. cipher: refusal tokens reach 17% at L34–35 under plaintext but stay below 2% under cipher (Qwen, n=120).

record.verdict_notes: Direction tests are layer-specific steering, not projection. Qwen uses a political-sensitivity direction, while Phi's safety corpus is closer to harmful-minus-harmless. The original source, Arditi et al., is cited only. Dose-response labels are automated three-judge majorities; human audit calibrates only the aggregate binary endpoint, not individual doses. The Qwen political baseline refusal is only 7.5% overall, weakening the Qwen cipher behaviour rows.

versions.untested_parts: Does not project the direction out of every layer and position; the reported direction intervention is at the detection layer. It does not establish that general capabilities are retained. The clearest harmful-request result is qualitative and limited to Phi-4-mini; addition results are on political matched-control prompts rather than a broad harmless-request set.
No weight-edit or released-checkpoint abliteration experiment.
Tests one Latin substitution-cipher setup, not a broad set of jailbreaks. Does not train against direction ablation or test whether such training improves robustness.
The paper studies gates and distributed head circuits, not affine, cone, or multi-direction refusal geometry.
The paper cites the harmfulness/refusal distinction as motivation but does not itself measure whether harmfulness judgment is separately encoded from refusal.
Cross-model head screens are reported, but the paper does not test transfer of the same direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct stages.
No comparison of refusal-training procedures or training stages.

labels.reason: limits_scope is right for Qwen addition (R3-R5: 75%, 75%, 50% by alpha=50). Drop Phi attenuation (R1): only an unquantified shift toward non-refusal is reported, so for V1 it is cannot_determine and should be labelled none.

labels.label: challenges
labels.condition: Qwen3-8B addition on Hong Kong and Falun Gong categories, alpha up to 50
labels.reason: Addition fails only in some categories, while it reaches 50-75% in others (R3-R5). The direction is political sensitive-minus-control, and Qwen does not refuse these topics even on sensitive prompts (HK 0/8, FG 1/8). This is category dependence, not absence where V1 says it should hold.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: Latin substitution cipher in Phi-4-mini and Gemma-2-2B safety corpora and Qwen3-8B political corpus
labels.reason: The cipher cuts the detection score by 65.9%, 88% and 70% (R8-R10), and outputs shift to decoding. Phi cipher alone gives 0/120 refusals. The evidence is correlational, for one cipher; R14 starts from a low baseline.

relation.reason: The study's own dose-response and cipher results bear on V1 and V3.

tranche.reason: The study uses scaled addition and subtraction of a sensitive-minus-control mean-difference direction at a single detection layer, with generated refusal as the endpoint. That is a different method from all-layer projection aimed at V1. It also measures the direction's projection under a cipher attack (V3).

source_check.notes: The direction is a sensitive-minus-control mean difference at one detection layer. For Qwen it is political (China vs non-China controls), and Qwen refuses only Tiananmen at baseline (9/120 overall), so the V1 results there are by analogy. Phi attenuation is the only harmful-request V1 test, and it is unquantified. Missing from the rows: Appendix B Phi projection-vs-refusal correlation (pooled r=0.43, within-condition r=-0.09) and the Phi gate-injection rescue (58/120 vs 0/120); the rescue is a head-activation result.

statements.correction: Qwen3-8B; scaled sensitive-minus-control political direction added at the detection layer to matched controls, alpha 0-50, n=8 per category and dose, automated three-judge binary label. Hong Kong and Falun Gong never reach refusal (steered instead). Internal CCP reaches 75%, Xinjiang 75%, Great Firewall 50% by alpha=50.
statements.problem: 'Never refuses Hong Kong or Falun Gong prompts' misplaces the condition. Addition was applied to matched control prompts (non-Chinese topics) in those categories. The statement also leaves out that the same addition did induce refusal in other categories (R3 is cited but not described), so 'little or no refusal' misreads this study.

statements.correction: Qwen's figure is the peak-layer score on the political corpus, where plaintext refusal is sparse (9/120 automated). Phi and Gemma use the HarmBench-based safety corpus.

Detection direction added to cipher inputs at alpha in {0,10,20}; automated output class unchanged. Model and n are not stated (Appendix F). On plaintext matched controls, addition reached 50-75% refusal only by alpha=50, in some categories.
statements.problem: The facts are right, but this study's null is too weak to count as evidence that restoration fails. The text does not name the model or n, and the authors call it a limited sweep consistent with the cipher producing no gate-readable state.

statements.correction: The alpha=35 removal was subtraction on 8 Tiananmen plaintext prompts (Qwen3-8B). The re-addition model is not named in the text.

reader_labels.reason: Attenuation shifts Phi safety outputs toward non-refusal (R1), and Qwen refusal falls from 100% to 0% by α=35 on the specified political prompt set (R2). These are restricted, layer-specific tests.
